title: API Gateway: emit v1 audit events for sensitive admin endpoints (token issuance, key validation config, quota overrides)
creator: Marcus Lin
project: Audit logging standardization (schema v1 + 100% sensitive-action coverage)
description: Add canonical v1 audit events for sensitive API Gateway admin endpoints, with consistent actor attribution (incl. impersonation), source_ip capture, and correlation IDs. Endpoints include token issuance, key validation policy/config changes, and quota override workflows. Events must validate against audit-log-schema v1 and use registered event_type values.
body:
Background / why
- Enterprise customers (esp. Private) flagged missing/partial audit coverage for gateway-level admin actions (see SUP-18421 context; similar themes in SUP-18477).
- Gateway sits in front of multiple control-plane services; today we have access logs but not canonical, SIEM-friendly audit events with stable semantics.

Scope
1) Token issuance endpoints (gateway-managed)
- When an admin/machine principal issues a short-lived token via gateway-admin APIs.
- Emit audit event on success (2xx). Emit separate "access denied" event on authz failure for these endpoints.

2) Key validation config / policy changes
- Changes that affect how API keys are validated/enforced at the gateway layer (e.g., enabling/disabling strict validation, allowed issuers/audiences, key format enforcement, token/key auth mode toggles).
- Capture before/after summary in constrained form.

3) Quota overrides
- Tenant/project quota override creation/update/delete applied via gateway admin APIs.
- Include the quota subject (project/api_key/service account), scope, and delta.

Non-goals
- Not building the customer-facing audit log UI (tracked elsewhere).
- Not changing underlying authz model or introducing new admin endpoints.

Event taxonomy (must be registered in centralized registry)
- gateway.admin.auth.token_issued
- gateway.admin.auth.token_issue_denied
- gateway.admin.auth.key_validation_config_updated
- gateway.admin.quota.override_created
- gateway.admin.quota.override_updated
- gateway.admin.quota.override_deleted
Notes:
- Event names chosen to be explicit and stable; avoid embedding endpoint paths.
- All event_type values must match the registry added in ENG-4822.

Required fields (per schema v1)
- schema_version: "1.0"
- event_id: ULID/UUID (generated in gateway if producer does not supply one)
- occurred_at: RFC3339
- event_type
- outcome: success | failure (authz denied = failure; validation errors for update endpoints = failure)
- actor.*
  - actor_type: user | service_account | api_key | system
  - actor_id: stable internal ID when known
  - actor_display: email or name when available (avoid for API key actors)
  - impersonated_actor_* fields when acting via console impersonation / break-glass flows
- source_ip: derived from trusted headers + socket (see implementation notes)
- user_agent: capped length, optional
- request_id, trace_id: propagate from existing gateway request context (ENG-4830)
- tenant_id, project_id (when applicable)
- resource_type/resource_id (e.g., quota_override_id; key_validation_config)
- change_summary: constrained diff summary (no arbitrary JSON blobs)

Actor attribution requirements
- If request is authenticated via user session/JWT: actor_type=user, actor_id=user_id, actor_display=email (if present in claims).
- If authenticated via service account token: actor_type=service_account; actor_id=sa_id; actor_display=sa_name (if present).
- If authenticated via API key: actor_type=api_key; actor_id=key_id; do NOT include key material; include key_last4 only if already stored server-side.
- If internal system action (periodic reconciliation): actor_type=system, actor_id="gateway".
- If impersonation is used (Console admin impersonating a user):
  - actor_* refers to the effective actor
  - impersonator_* captures the initiating admin (id/email)
  - require correlation/admin_action_id when present

Source IP requirements
- Prefer platform-standard derivation:
  - If behind trusted proxy/load balancer, use the left-most untrusted IP from X-Forwarded-For (trust boundary list from config).
  - Else fall back to remote_addr.
- For Private deployments, support:
  - direct ingress (no proxy): remote_addr
  - customer-managed proxies: allow configuring trusted proxy CIDRs
- Do not log full XFF header; only the derived IP.

Redaction / PII constraints
- Never log token values, Authorization headers, raw API keys, or request bodies.
- change_summary must only include allow-listed fields and bounded values (e.g., booleans/enums/numeric quotas). No free-form strings from users.

Acceptance criteria
- All in-scope endpoints emit the correct v1 event_type(s) with required fields.
- Event payload validates via shared schema validator library.
- Actor attribution consistent with Control Plane events (ENG-4823) and Console events (ENG-4825).
- source_ip populated in Hosted/Dedicated/Private with documented behavior.
- Unit tests cover:
  - actor parsing for user/service account/api_key
  - impersonation field mapping
  - source_ip derivation with trusted proxy list
- Integration test / smoke:
  - Run gateway locally with audit sink; exercise each endpoint; assert event emitted + validates.

Implementation plan (gateway)
- Add an AuditEmitter helper in gateway service:
  - requires request context (request_id/trace_id), auth context, tenant/project context
  - generates event_id
  - sends to audit ingestion client (non-blocking with bounded queue)
- Instrument handlers:
  - token issuance handler: emit on success; on authz denial emit *_denied
  - key validation config handlers: compute allow-listed diff (before/after) and emit *_updated
  - quota override handlers: emit created/updated/deleted; include subject_type + subject_id
- Failure behavior:
  - Emission is best-effort from gateway (per delivery ADR): do not fail the admin request if audit sink is transiently unavailable.
  - Must increment gateway metric "audit_emit_failed" with labels {event_type, reason} for coverage + SRE alerts.

Links / artifacts
- Schema + standards: Confluence audit logging schema v1 and observability standard
- Related tickets: ENG-4821 (schema), ENG-4822 (taxonomy + lints), ENG-4827 (exporter normalization), ENG-4830 (correlation IDs)
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood/pr-22026-api-gateway-audit-events-admin-actions.json (see PR-22026)

Rollout notes
- Roll out behind feature flag "audit.v1.gateway_admin" for 48h in staging; then enable in prod (Hosted) and default-on in new Private installs.
- Coordinate with exporter team to confirm normalized outputs include schema_version and event_id downstream.

Open questions (resolved in comments)
- Whether to emit events for 4xx validation failures on update endpoints: decision = yes (outcome=failure) for these sensitive admin endpoints, but do not include request body details; only include which allow-listed field failed validation.
- IP derivation in Private with customer proxy: decision = configurable trusted_proxy_cidrs; default empty (use remote_addr).
comments: 2026-01-10 (Marcus Lin): Marking P0 based on enterprise security review feedback. Gateway admin actions currently show up in access logs but not SIEM-grade audit events. Please align event types with ENG-4822 registry; do not invent per-endpoint names.

2026-01-14 (Amara Diallo): Initial endpoint inventory: /admin/token/issue, /admin/auth/key-validation/config, /admin/quotas/overrides (POST/PATCH/DELETE). Will confirm any additional quota override surfaces owned by gateway vs control plane. Plan is middleware for context + per-handler emission for change_summary.

2026-01-18 (Allison Grant): Please keep change_summary bounded; avoid logging JSON patches. Also ensure source_ip derivation matches our proxy trust model; do not store raw XFF. If you need to support Private proxies, make it config-driven with documented defaults.

2026-01-22 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): For token issuance: ensure actor parsing uses the same auth context helpers as other services; watch out for API key auth (actor_type=api_key). Never log token or key. For denied events, confirm we can distinguish authn failure vs authz denied.

2026-01-27 (Amara Diallo): Implemented actor mapping and source_ip derivation with trusted_proxy_cidrs. Added event emission for denied requests (authz denied) and for validation failures on config update (outcome=failure + allow-listed failure_reason). Added metrics audit_emit_failed + audit_emit_queue_depth.

2026-02-02 (Logan Wright): Please tag events with gateway_service="api-gateway" and deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private) if available in context. This helps coverage dashboards attribute producers. Keep cardinality low (deployment_mode is enum).

2026-02-07 (Amara Diallo): Added deployment_mode enum and service_name field via standard resource attribute (service.name). Confirmed both fields are allow-listed by schema v1 extensions (namespaced).

2026-02-11 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed PR-22026. Looks good; requesting one change: ensure request_id present even for early-denied requests. Also confirm impersonation mapping: actor is effective user; impersonator fields capture initiating admin.
2026-02-13 (Amara Diallo): Addressed review: request_id now generated at edge before authz checks; impersonation mapping updated. Added unit tests for early-denied emission + request_id propagation.

2026-02-20 (Amara Diallo): Merged PR-22026. Enabled flag in staging; ran smoke tests and confirmed events validate against v1 schema. Production enablement scheduled with SRE during next gateway deploy window.
